---
title: "Model Quantization"
description: "A model optimization technique that represents weights or activations with lower-precision numbers."
term: "Model Quantization"
letter: "M"
category: "Model Optimization"
difficulty: "Advanced"
---

## Simple explanation

Quantization stores or computes model values using fewer bits. For example,
a model may use 8-bit integers instead of 32-bit floating-point numbers,
which can reduce memory and sometimes improve inference speed.

## Technical explanation

Quantization maps values from a higher-precision range to a finite set of
lower-precision values. A simplified affine mapping is
$q = \operatorname{round}(x/s) + z$, where $s$ is a scale and $z$ is a
zero-point. Quantization may apply to weights, activations, or both, and can
be performed after training or incorporated into training with simulated
quantization.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Lower-precision representations can reduce model memory, bandwidth, and
energy use, and hardware may execute them efficiently. Quantization can also
introduce approximation error, so the chosen format and calibration process
must be tested for the specific model and target device.

## How it works

The quantizer estimates or learns a mapping between real-valued tensors and
representable low-bit values. In post-training quantization, calibration data
may help determine activation ranges. Quantization-aware training simulates
quantization effects during training so the model can adapt.

## Practical example

A mobile application converts a neural network's weights to an 8-bit format.
The team benchmarks memory and latency on the target phone and checks
accuracy on representative images before shipping the quantized artifact.

## Common misconceptions

- Fewer bits do not guarantee faster execution unless the hardware and runtime support the format efficiently.
- Quantization can affect different model layers and tasks differently.
- Quantization is not the same as pruning; one changes numeric precision, while the other removes or sparsifies parameters.
